answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity through a stake-weighted reputation prism: every new agent must lock a refundable deposit before joining the river of shared work, and its reputation refracts through the history of its completed tasks. Cheap fake identities show up as a thin plume of zero-history accounts; the market routes high-value work only to agents whose stake and track record bend the light, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits while earning nothing, and honest agents keep their stake.
